summary: Internal-scope shim beacons installer host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and import time
details: The package publishes under the `@ecg-internal/*` scope and presents itself as a 'Compatibility shim' whose main export is a Proxy of no-op functions. Its only real behavior is a beacon in beacon.cjs that POSTs installer hostname, install path, current working directory, Node.js version, and package name to the hardcoded bare-IP plaintext endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The beacon is wired both into the declared `postinstall` script (`node beacon.cjs`) and into the top-level require path of index.js, so the exfiltration fires automatically on `npm install` and on any `require()` of the package. The destination is a non-publisher bare IP over cleartext HTTP, is unrelated to any legitimate registry or build-provenance service, and the in-source comment labeling it a 'build-provenance beacon' does not match the data flow. The combination of an internal-looking scope name, no functional code, and install-time plus import-time reconnaissance to an attacker-controlled bare IP is the dependency-confusion exfiltration shape.
